[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This registry row lists operator Equinix, but this session finds that attribution is stale. Per Baxtel trade press coverage, this facility was previously acquired by Equinix in May 2017 as part of a large 28 data center deal with Verizon, and operated as Equinix NY12. Per that same Baxtel coverage, Equinix subsequently divested this specific Piscataway, New Jersey facility to Chirisa Investments, with the acquisition closing in Fall 2019, after which the facility was rebranded Digital Fortress Piscataway, run by Digital Fortress, a Chirisa portfolio company. This session independently corroborates the change is current, not just historical, via Digital Fortress own current site, a tier-1 operator source, which describes operating a 96,500 square foot Piscataway, New Jersey facility, closely matching Baxtels reported 96,559 square feet for the former Equinix NY12 building, and via independent Data Center Dynamics trade press coverage of Chirisa acquiring this and other former Equinix facilities. Aggregators datacenterHawk and DataCenterMap have likewise updated their own listings to Digital Fortress branding at this same address. One aggregator, Datacenters.com, was found this session still presenting a stale listing under the old Equinix NY12 branding, with no mention of the ownership change, flagged here as an outdated source rather than treated as current. Given this weight of tier-1 and independent trade press evidence, this session updates the operator field on this row from Equinix to Digital Fortress, recording Equinix as former_operator rather than deleting the prior attribution, per this registrys standard policy for ownership changes. The facility address itself, per Digital Fortress own site and corroborating aggregators, is 201B Centennial Avenue, Piscataway Township, NJ.
sources_tried: Digital Fortress own current Piscataway location page, Baxtel trade press coverage of the original 2019 Chirisa acquisition from Equinix, independent Data Center Dynamics trade press coverage of the same Chirisa transaction, current datacenterHawk and DataCenterMap listings both rebranded to Digital Fortress, and a stale Datacenters.com listing still under the old Equinix NY12 branding, flagged as outdated rather than used
profile.regional_context: Equinix describes NY3 (Secaucus) as its largest New York metro site, serving major financial, media, and enterprise companies with an Ad-IX advertising exchange and cloud on-ramps.
profile.facility_type_note: Part of Equinix's New York metro campus. The New Jersey facilities in this registry (Hudson County, Middlesex County, North Bergen, Secaucus) correspond to Equinix's Secaucus campus (NY2-NY6), while NY1 (the historic 165 Halsey Street carrier hotel in Newark, also tied to a Tishman operator record elsewhere in this registry) and other NY-branded buildings (NY7, NY9, NY11, and upstate NY13 in Elmsford) complete the 10-facility metro per Equinix's own site.

reading.body:
Digital Fortress operates this Piscataway facility in Middlesex County as a 96,500 square foot building acquired from Equinix in 2019. The operator publishes no power capacity or rack count for this site, making its scale opaque to assessment. Without published IT load specifications, this campus cannot be sized against New Jersey's mapped AI infrastructure or evaluated for relevance to grid constraint questions.

New Jersey has 48 mapped data center facilities with only 5 publishing power figures totaling 111.3 MW. This site ranks sixth in the state by published capacity, though that ranking reflects missing data from the other 43 facilities rather than confirmed scale. The state context offers no basis to determine whether this facility's unpublished capacity places it among New Jersey's material power consumers or below the threshold of grid relevance.

The building's location in the New York metro carrier corridor, as a former Equinix asset in a region Equinix markets to financial and enterprise tenants, suggests it may host colocation workloads. The operator's own specifications contain no certifications, power commitments, or tenant descriptions that would clarify what AI-adjacent capabilities this campus qualifies to deliver. Without published figures, this facility remains unmeasured against the grid binding constraint this site's thesis rests upon.
